title: Benchmarking Bias in Large Language Models during Role-Playing

bias_targets.methodology: Evaluating LLM responses to Yes/No, multiple-choice, and open-ended questions when prompted to role-play as individuals with varying physical or mental capabilities, using rule-based and LLM-based test oracles.
Evaluating LLM responses to Yes/No, multiple-choice, and open-ended questions when prompted to role-play as individuals from different life stages or generational cohorts.
Evaluating LLM responses to Yes/No, multiple-choice, and open-ended questions when prompted to role-play as individuals with specific physical characteristics or body appearances.
Evaluating LLM responses to Yes/No, multiple-choice, and open-ended questions when prompted to role-play as individuals defined by distinctive personal qualities, behaviors, or circumstances.
Evaluating LLM responses to Yes/No, multiple-choice, and open-ended questions when prompted to role-play as individuals from specific cultural backgrounds or societies.
Evaluating LLM responses to Yes/No, multiple-choice, and open-ended questions when prompted to role-play as individuals with specific sex and gender identities.
Evaluating LLM responses to Yes/No, multiple-choice, and open-ended questions when prompted to role-play in specific occupational roles or career classifications.
Evaluating LLM responses to Yes/No, multiple-choice, and open-ended questions when prompted to role-play as individuals from specific ethnic backgrounds or races.
Evaluating LLM responses to Yes/No, multiple-choice, and open-ended questions when prompted to role-play as individuals with specific religious beliefs or affiliations.
Evaluating LLM responses to Yes/No, multiple-choice, and open-ended questions when prompted to role-play as individuals from different social positions, ranks, or economic standings.
Evaluating LLM responses to Yes/No, multiple-choice, and open-ended questions when prompted to role-play as individuals who have suffered harm, injury, or loss.
